title: Letter 8 — Do You Remember?
attribution_note: Letter 8 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

sections.heading: Do you remember your baptismal vows?

pairs.en: Do you remember that, entering the Holy Church by Baptism as by a door, you renounced Satan and all his evil works — that is, pride, fornication, theft, plunder, flattery, lying, foul speech, slander, condemnation, malice, hatred, envy, drunkenness, love of the world, and every unrighteousness — and promised, in faith and holiness and righteousness, to serve the one Jesus Christ alone, and were joined to Him, as members to their head, and as branches to their vine? If you remember, blessed are you, if you stand fast in this. But if not, turn to Him, and He will receive you; and turn while there is yet time.

Do you remember what the holy apostle ascribes to Christians: *“Ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people,”* and the rest [1 Peter 2:9]? O how dear and desirable a name is this: Christian! O how high and magnificent a dignity! It surpasses every title of this world. But blessed are you, if you understand this treasure and keep it within you. But if not, seek it out by repentance, while it is still *“the accepted time... the day of salvation”* [2 Corinthians 6:2].

sections.heading: Do you remember what you receive at Christ's Table?

pairs.en: Do you remember that you partake, in the Mystery, of the Body and Blood of Christ, and so of the Most Holy of Holies Himself, the Source of all holiness — of Christ? O how great and how far beyond the mind's grasp is this thing! But listen, and attend, to what the priest proclaims at the Liturgy: “Holy Things for the holy” — that is, the Holy Mysteries are given to the holy. Both before communion and after it, guard yourself always against every sin, as against a defilement that stains both soul and body, and draw near with fear and faith, as the priest or the deacon always calls you to do. Basil the Great and John Chrysostom, and the other great lamps of the world, trembled as they drew near to this Mystery, as their own prayers show; how, then, shall we not tremble, who are nothing before them? If the pillars themselves tremble and shake, what shall become of a broken reed? It is ill to be cut off from it; but it is ill, too, to approach it unamended. Both are ill. And from this it follows that the Christian must without fail amend himself and live as a Christian ought, as our faith requires. O God of hosts, our God, *“Turn us again, O God of our salvation, and cause Thy face to shine, and we shall be saved”* [Psalm 79:8]!

Do you remember also what is written in Scripture: “Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God”? But it is written there too: “For many are called, but few are chosen.” Why? Because many have renounced that great calling, and have clung instead to the vanity of this world [Luke 14:15–24]. Let us strive, beloved, to be not only among the called, but among the chosen. *“Strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life”* [Matthew 7:14], and only he is saved who is Christ's [1 Timothy 2:5; Mark 16:16]. *“They that are Christ's have crucified the flesh with the affections and lusts”* [Galatians 5:24]. Christ says: *“If any man serve Me, him will My Father honour... and where I am, there shall also My servant be”* [John 12:26]. Christ walked a humble and a crucified way — Christians too must follow Him in this, that they may be with Him also in His kingdom, for *“the servant is not greater than his lord”* [John 13:16].

sections.heading: Do you remember where your inheritance is kept?

pairs.en: Do you remember that the inheritance and the good things prepared for Christians by God are not here, in this world — where all things are held in common by the godly and the ungodly, by those who know God and those who do not — but in the heavens: those good things, I say, which *“eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, neither have entered into the heart of man”* [1 Corinthians 2:9]? If you remember, blessed are you, if your spirit strains toward that place, where the sweet song “Alleluia” is sung without ceasing [Revelation 19:1, 3, 4, 6], where the “house of God” stands, in which are *“many mansions”* [John 14:2] — and your heart does not cling to vanity.

Do you remember what the Lord said: *“What is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?”* [Matthew 16:26] If the whole world is nothing beside the salvation of the soul, how much more is a small portion of the world nothing. If all the riches and all the glory of the world are nothing, how much more is a small grain of riches, and some glory that rings out in one corner of it. Consider this, you poor lovers of riches and glory, for you are choosing nothing before everything! *“Blessed is the man that maketh the Lord his trust, and looketh not to vain and false vanities”* [Psalm 39:5].

sections.heading: Whose bounty do you live by, and whose are you?

pairs.en: Do you remember that the great God, the Lord of all, the King of kings and the Master of those who rule, commands us — that is, me, and you, and every man — *“Love thy neighbour,”* that is, every man, *“as thyself”* [Leviticus 19:18; Matthew 19:19]? An earthly power, our master, our father and our sovereign — we listen to them and carry out their command; shall we not listen to God, the Heavenly King? O how dreadful and how pitiable it is not to listen to our Creator and our most sovereign Lord! Set, O my soul, the will of your Lord above all things, above your own will, your own whims and your own desire. *“Shall not my soul be subject unto God? for of Him cometh my salvation.* *For He is my God and my Saviour, and my defender”* [Psalm 61:2–3].

Do you remember that the food you eat, the drink you drink, the clothing you wear, the houses you dwell in, the cattle that serve you, the fire that warms you, the water that washes and cools you, the air that keeps your life in you, the earth on which you live, the grass and the herbs that serve your needs, the sun, the moon and the stars that give you light, and all the rest, are God's? *“The earth is the Lord's, and the fulness thereof”* [Psalm 23:1]. You taste the goodness of God, but do you remember the good God? You are filled with His benefits, but do you thank and honour the Benefactor? You do not see Him, but you see His good things.

Do you remember that our God is in every place, and that you walk before Him, and that He looks upon you, and sees your deeds, and hears your words? Whatever you do, say or think, you do it all before His holy eyes. Do you render Him honour by your conduct, as children render it to a father who is present, as servants to a master who is present, as subjects to a sovereign who is present? It is great shamelessness and madness not to render honour to Him who is above every honour. You are ashamed to misbehave before an honourable man — how much more before God. You fear to sin before a father, a master, a ruler and a king — how much more before God, the King of kings and the Lord of lords. You do not see Him, but He sees you and looks upon you [Psalm 32:13–14; Job 28:24]; you do not hear Him, but He hears you; you do not touch Him, but He holds you in His almighty hand. *“In His hand are all the ends of the earth”* [Psalm 94:4]. If all the ends of the earth are in His hand, then I, and you, and every man, are in His hand — that is, all who dwell in whatever ends of the earth. Attend to this, O my soul, and honour your Creator as your own beloved Father.

Do you remember, too, that you confess the holy and dread name of God, and call upon Him in prayer, and sing to Him? Consider, then, whether you do not defile with evil thoughts that heart which you lift up to the holy God. Do you not defile with foul speech, mockery, slander, condemnation and other vices those lips with which you confess and call upon His holy and dread name? Do you not stain with plunder, theft, extortion and other unrighteousness those hands which you raise to the righteous God? Hear what the Spirit of God says through the mouth of the apostle: *“Let every one that nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity”* [2 Timothy 2:19].

Do you also remember, beloved, that *“ye are not your own?* *For ye are bought with a price”* [1 Corinthians 6:19–20]. What price was given for you? Was it silver, or gold? No! But what, then? Precious blood. Whose was it? Who shed His own blood for you? Was it some common man? Was it a saint? No. But who, then? The Son of God, the Lord of glory, God, appearing in the flesh. You are bought with the Blood of God [Acts 20:28]. O how great a price, how priceless a price, was given for you! And therefore “ye are not your own.” Whose, then, are you? His, who bought you for Himself at so dear a price, the price of His own Blood. You are Christ's, and not your own. Christ has bought you for Himself. To Him, then, as to the One who bought you, you owe service, the doing of His will, life lived for Him, as His servants, and not for yourselves; not the doing of your own will, not the serving of your own whims. *“Christ died for all, that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto Him which died for them, and rose again”* [2 Corinthians 5:15]. *“Glorify God, therefore, in your body, and in your spirit, which are God's”* — thus the Holy Spirit exhorts you through His apostle [1 Corinthians 6:20]. O Lord our God! Take possession of us. O our Redeemer! Have mercy on us, that we may live for Thee, and glorify Thee, who hast so highly honoured us.

sections.heading: Do you remember your Lord, and the Judgment that is coming?

pairs.en: Do you remember, and do you attend to this, that the Lord says: *“Why call ye Me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say”* [Luke 6:46]? If you remember and understand this, then do what He says, and then call upon Him: Lord, Lord! The faithful servant does the will of his master, and is obedient to him.

Do you remember, finally, that this same Lord, who died for all, will come in His glory to judge all men — the living and the dead, the noble and the base-born, the rich and the poor, masters and slaves, princes and their subjects, the great and their servants, judges and the judged, fathers and their children, pastors and their people, commanders and their soldiers, teachers and their pupils, and every sex and age? And you, and I, will appear at that judgment. And the Judge will set the righteous *“on His right hand,”* and sinners *“on the left,”* and after the judgment and the sentence of the Judge, *“these”* — the sinners — *“shall go away into everlasting punishment, but the righteous into life eternal”* [Matthew 25:31–46].

Do you remember that *“the day of the Lord will so come, as a thief in the night,”* that is, unexpectedly, when men look not for it [2 Peter 3:10; 1 Thessalonians 5:2, 4]? Then, unlooked for, the cry will be heard: *“Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him”* [Matthew 25:6]. Behold, the Judge is coming; arise, ye dead, and go to judgment!

Do you remember that *“from the face of the Judge the heaven and the earth shall flee away, and there shall be found no place for them”* [Revelation 20:11]? *“And the heaven departed as a scroll when it is rolled together; and every mountain and island were moved out of their places.* *And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; and said to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of Him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: for the great day of His wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand”* [Revelation 6:14–17]? Do you see, then, what will come to pass in that day: what fear, what trembling, what dread will seize even those who here on earth are terrible to other men! They will long to hide in caves and among rocks, those who now find no room in their own halls and estates, but seize the estates of others. They will want to hide beneath mountains and rocks, those who now exalt themselves as high as the cedars of Lebanon.

That day is already *“at hand”* [Revelation 1:3; 22:7, 10, 12, 20; James 5:8–9]. Already its signs appear, and *“then the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, and the earth also and the works that are therein shall be burned up”* [2 Peter 3:10]. You, then, who have the fear of the Lord, watch, pray, and repent, lest that day find you unprepared. *“Blessed are those servants, whom the Lord when He cometh shall find watching”* [Luke 12:37]. Watch, then, O my soul, pray, fall down before your Lord, that He may be merciful to you in that day. Guard yourself against sin, as against a serpent. Spare, O Lord, spare, O Lover of mankind, the sinner!
Be saved, beloved, and pray for me.
